skill.name: Who is it aimed at, and what do they want?
skill.why: Every persuasive text has a target. Know who, and you'll see the push.
skill.how: Find clues in the words, places and prices. Then ask what the reader should do.

beats.say: Every persuasive text is aimed at someone.
Look for clues about who the reader is.
beats.show: **Parents!** Pack a healthy snack in **your child's lunchbox**.

beats.say: Prices, places and favourite things are clues too.
Then ask: what does the writer want them to do?
If it's aimed at you, ask: is it good for me?

encounters.text: Dear families, is your child nervous in the water? Do they cling to the side of the pool, or refuse to put their face in? You're not alone, and we can help. This summer, the Bluster Rock pool is running Little Splashers, a gentle learn-to-swim program for children aged 4 to 8. Classes have no more than four children, so every child gets plenty of attention. Our teachers are patient, kind and trained to work with nervous swimmers. You can watch every lesson from the shaded viewing deck, with a free coffee from the kiosk. Lessons run on weekday mornings for two weeks in January and cost $90 for the whole program. Living on an island means your child will spend a lot of time near water, so learning to swim is one of the best gifts you can give them. Places are limited, so please book at the pool office before 15 December.

encounters.text: The Bluster Rock bakery has launched three new products this month. The first is a high-protein muesli bar, made with oats, nuts and seeds. The second is a pack of frozen mini pizzas that can be heated in five minutes. The third is a fruit loaf baked from an old family recipe, which can be wrapped and posted. The bakery wrote a separate ad for each product, aimed at a different group of customers. Mo cut the ads into strips to make a guessing game for the crew, but he forgot which strip came from which ad. Indi says the clues in each line are enough to sort them out. The muesli bars cost $3 each and come in honey or chocolate. The mini pizzas come in packs of six. The fruit loaf is wrapped in brown paper and tied with string, and it stays fresh for two weeks. Gus guessed every line wrong on purpose, so he could eat the prizes.

encounters.frame: Wren's wildlife shelter wrote a letter to the island's truck drivers. Tully summed it up, but got one part wrong.
encounters.text: Dear truck drivers of Bluster Rock, every week, our shelter cares for wombats, wallabies and echidnas that have been hit by vehicles on the coast road. Most of these accidents happen at dusk and dawn, when animals are moving to and from their burrows. Many of you drive this road every day, and we know you care about the island as much as we do. We are asking you to do one simple thing: please slow down to 60 kilometres an hour on the coast road between 5 pm and 7 am. If you do hit an animal, please don't try to pick it up yourself, because injured wombats can bite and scratch. Instead, call the shelter's 24-hour rescue line, which is printed on the sticker we've attached to this letter. Thank you for helping us keep our wildlife safe. From Wren and the volunteers at the Bluster Rock Wildlife Shelter.

encounters.text: 'What's up, Vantafam! Maxx here, and this is the MaxxCam Rocket Kit! Build your very own gold rocket, launch it in your backyard, and film the whole thing with the tiny camera in the nose. It flies up to 100 metres, which is higher than any rocket your friends have. encounters.frame: The Bluster Rock tourism office has printed a glossy new brochure. Tully is reading it aloud in a very dramatic voice.
encounters.text: WINTER ON BLUSTER ROCK: YOUR TIME, AT LAST. The kids have left home, the alarm clock is a thing of the past, and the open road is calling. Why spend another cold, grey winter in the city when you could be watching the sun go down over the red rock, with a cup of tea in your hand and nowhere to be in the morning? Bluster Rock's caravan park has sixty powered sites, each with its own water tap and a shady tree, plus hot showers, a laundry and a camp kitchen. Stay for a week, a month or the whole season: the longer you stay, the cheaper each night becomes, and holders of a seniors' card save a further 15 per cent. Our winter days are warm and dry, averaging 22 degrees, so you can leave the heavy coats at home. Join the morning walking group, try the Tuesday lawn bowls, or simply sit by the camp fire and swap stories with fellow travellers from all over the country. Many of our winter guests have been returning every year for over a decade, and they say the island feels like a second home. Book your site now, before the best spots by the water are taken.

parts: The program, called Throw One Back, asks you to release any snapper shorter than 40 centimetres, even though the legal size is 30. encounters.frame: A robot vacuum company has written three ads for the same machine, each aimed at different customers. Gus has the strips spread across the galley table.
encounters.text: The Dustwhisker 9 is a small robot vacuum that cleans floors on its own, then returns to its charging dock. It has a filter that traps fine dust and pollen, a brush that untangles long hair, and a quiet mode that is no louder than a whisper. It can be set to run at any time of day from a phone. Its maker wrote three separate ads for it, each aimed at a different kind of customer, and printed them as strips of paper for a shop display. The Dustwhisker 9 costs $480, comes with a two-year guarantee, and can clean a three-bedroom house on a single charge. Its bin holds a full week of dust, and a small light glows orange when the bin needs emptying. Before they were stuck up, a gust of wind blew them off the counter, and the shop assistant asked Gus to put them back in the right piles. Gus says it's the most useful thing anyone has ever asked him to do. He has also asked whether the Dustwhisker can be trained to pick up slime, and the shop assistant has stopped answering his questions. Mo asked if it could clean up after his cooking. The assistant laughed, then realised he was serious.

encounters.frame: A new escape room has opened in the old Bluster Rock bank. Indi wrote a note about its ad, but got one part wrong.
encounters.text: THE VAULT: AN ESCAPE ROOM FOR TEAMS THAT MEAN BUSINESS. Is your office running on autopilot? Do your colleagues only talk to each other in emails? Bring your workplace team to The Vault, where you'll have sixty minutes to escape a haunted bank vault before the ghost of its last manager returns from his lunch break. Solving our puzzles takes clear communication, quick decisions and real trust, the very same skills your team needs back at the office. Groups of six to twelve can book weekday sessions from 9 am to 5 pm, and we can send an invoice directly to your business. Many local companies now use The Vault for staff training days, and our meeting room is available for a debrief over coffee and pastries afterwards. Please note that The Vault is not suitable for children under 16, as some puzzles take place in near-darkness and involve a recorded scream that is, frankly, quite loud. Sessions cost $45 per person, and a team photo in the vault is included. Gift vouchers are available at the front desk for managers who want to reward a hard-working team.

encounters.frame: An email from Maxx arrived on the crew's tablet. Zed is reading it with his eyebrows getting higher and higher.
encounters.text: 'Hey there, Vantafam juniors! It's your favourite streamer, Maxx Vantablack, with a top-secret invitation just for you. I'm starting the Vantafam Kids' Club, and only my biggest fans aged 8 to 12 are invited. Club members get a gold badge for their gaming profile, early access to my new game, Gold Rush Racers, and a special birthday surprise from me every single year. Joining is super easy and totally free. Just fill in the form below with your full name, your birthday, your home address and the name of your school, so I know where to send your surprise. You don't need to bother your parents with this. It's just between us, Vantafam! The first 500 members will also get their name read out on my Saturday stream. Hurry, because spots are filling up fast! Smash that heart button like it owes you money, and stay gold!' At the bottom of the email, in tiny grey writing, it says that all details collected will be shared with Vantamart's partners. Wren went very quiet, then said she'd seen this trick before. Zed deleted the email and blocked the address.

encounters.frame: The Bluster Rock gallery has sent out an invitation to a new exhibition. Indi wants to go. The Pitchling isn't sure she's who it's for.
encounters.prompt: Tap the sentence that most clearly shows who the invitation is aimed at.
encounters.success: Prices from $4,000 and talk of investments speak to wealthy art collectors, not to everyday visitors like Indi.

parts: THE RED EARTH COLLECTION: AN EXCLUSIVE PREVIEW EVENING. The Bluster Rock Gallery invites you to a private preview of twenty-four new paintings by island artist Mara Quill, whose desert landscapes have been exhibited in galleries across the country.

parts.tap: Each painting captures the changing colours of the rock, from the pale pink of dawn to the deep crimson of sunset.
parts.reason: This describes the art. Anyone who likes paintings could enjoy reading it.

parts.tap: The preview evening begins at 6 pm on Friday 9 May, with drinks served in the courtyard.
parts.reason: A time and drinks could suit many guests. It doesn't narrow down who's invited.

parts.tap: With prices starting at $4,000, these original works are a sound investment for the serious collector.
Mara Quill will give a short talk about her painting methods at 7 pm.
parts.reason: An artist's talk could interest students, artists or collectors. It isn't a clear clue.

parts: Mara Quill grew up on a sheep station at the foot of the rock and taught herself to paint with house paint on old fence palings. Her largest work in this collection is three metres wide and took eighteen months to finish. Guests who reserve a painting on the night will receive a signed print and free delivery anywhere in Australia. Numbers are strictly limited, so please reply to this invitation by 1 May. The exhibition opens to the public the following Saturday, when entry will be free for everyone. Indi has decided to go on Saturday instead, with her sketchbook and a packed lunch.
